inputs.notes: FCF is normalised FCF from operations (Underlying EBITDA minus maintenance capex, cash interest, cash tax). Reported FCF is negative due to development capex which is excluded from this DCF. Net debt = total bank debt $627.7m minus cash $7.6m. Fiscal year ends March 31.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (13.11%) diverges from Revenue 5yr CAGR (6.12%) by 7.0pp. This is explained by significant capital raises and equity issuance between FY2020 and FY2022 (equity grew from $595m to $949m), not organic earnings growth. EPS and reported FCF CAGRs are not meaningful due to fair value movements and development capex respectively. EBITDA 3yr CAGR (4.12%) used as selected rate - most representative of recent operating trajectory.
historical_growth.notes: FY2021 was a 10-month period (balance date change from May to March) and is excluded from CAGR calculations. Reported FCF is negative in all years due to heavy development capex (ORA model). Normalised FCF from operations uses Underlying EBITDA minus maintenance capex (~$22-25m), cash interest (~$28m), and cash tax (~$4m). 3yr period: FY2022-FY2025. 5yr period: FY2020-FY2025.

base.description: Moderate recovery. Cost savings partially flow through FY26 ($13.2m of $20.4m), fully from FY27. The Helier achieves full cash recovery by mid-FY26. Development restarts at ~100 units/year from FY27. Care EBITDA per bed continues improving toward $15k+ average. Interest rates fall as RBNZ OCR settles around 2.25-2.75%. Gearing reduces to ~30% by FY28.

bull.description: Strong execution. All $20.4m cost savings achieved and flowing by FY27. NZ property market recovery lifts ORA prices 5-8% per annum. Care EBITDA per bed reaches $15k+ across full portfolio by FY28. Development ramps to 150 units/year from FY27 with 35% development margins. The Helier fully sold Q1 FY26. Divestment proceeds ($40m) deployed to reduce debt rapidly. RBNZ rate cuts reduce interest costs meaningfully.

bear.description: Weak execution. NZ property market stalls or declines, suppressing ORA demand and development margins. The Helier remains slow through FY26, delaying debt reduction. Government aged care funding insufficient to offset cost inflation. Cost savings partially achieved but offset by revenue headwinds. Development deferred beyond FY27. Gearing remains above 35%, limiting flexibility. Possible equity raise if covenant headroom tightens.

sensitivity.notes: Matrix shows intrinsic value per share (NZD) for base case FCF projections across varying WACC and terminal growth rate assumptions. Current price $0.72 is above intrinsic value in most scenarios - model is sensitive to WACC given the high net debt ($620m) relative to equity value.

probability_weighted.commentary: Probability-weighted intrinsic value of $0.75 is broadly in line with current price of $0.72, suggesting fair to slight undervaluation. The bear case equity value is negative due to the high net debt ($620m) relative to DCF enterprise value under stressed assumptions - this reflects the genuine financial leverage risk in the business. The wide range of outcomes ($-0.07 to $1.49) underscores that OCA.NZ is a leveraged recovery play where execution risk is high.

key_metrics.ev_ebitda_note: Enterprise Value ~$1,192m base case / FY25 EBITDA $86m = ~13.9x EV/EBITDA at base IV. Current market EV = market cap $521m + net debt $620m = $1,141m = 13.3x FY25 EBITDA

dcf_methodology_notes.fcf_approach: This DCF uses Normalised FCF from Operations, defined as Underlying EBITDA minus maintenance capex, cash interest and cash tax. Reported Free Cash Flow (which includes development capex) is negative in most years and is NOT used as the DCF input - development capex is growth investment that generates future ORA receipts, not a recurring cash cost.
dcf_methodology_notes.wacc_rationale: Base WACC of 9% reflects: NZ risk-free rate ~4.0% (10yr NZ Govt bond), equity risk premium ~5%, sector beta ~0.9, plus size/illiquidity premium. Range of 8-12% tested in sensitivity analysis. Bear case uses 11% to reflect elevated financial leverage.
dcf_methodology_notes.terminal_growth_rationale: Terminal growth of 3.0% in base case reflects NZ nominal GDP growth (~2.5%) plus demographic-driven volume growth for aged care. Bull case 3.5% reflects accelerating demand as 75+ cohort grows faster post-2030. Bear case 2.5% reflects subdued growth if property market and government funding remain headwinds.
dcf_methodology_notes.net_debt_treatment: Net debt of $620.1m deducted from enterprise value to derive equity value. This is material relative to market cap (~$521m) and creates significant sensitivity - a $100m change in net debt moves intrinsic value by $0.14/share.
dcf_methodology_notes.development_capex_excluded: Development capex (building new retirement village units) is treated as growth investment, not captured in the normalised FCF. The DCF therefore values the existing portfolio as a going concern. Future development creates additional value but this is not modelled.
dcf_methodology_notes.fy2021_exclusion: FY2021 was a 10-month period following a balance date change from May 31 to March 31. It is excluded from CAGR calculations to avoid distortion.
